mainTopic: טרפות of the internal organs: needles, pits and holes in the lung, the ruling against רבי שמעון, and the fat on the קֵבָה.
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of needles and pits found inside an animal's organs. Checking which way a needle's eye faces is valid evidence, except in the stomach, where food and drink can push a needle around. רבינא rules that a needle in the liver's big duct leaves the animal כשרה. A date pit in the gallbladder is assumed to have slipped in through the duct, but a pointed olive pit may have pierced it. After a side remark that a lung prepared with special substances is good for the eyes, the גמרא rules that a hole in the lung where the butcher handled it is blamed on him, just as we blame a wolf. A worm hole is also assumed to have formed after שחיטה. Then the גמרא sorts out conflicting reports of whether the הלכה follows רבי שמעון on lung holes, and rules that it does not. Finally, it turns to the fat on the קֵבָה, which the כהנים ate following רבי ישמעאל. Along the way it explains his reading of ברכת כהנים, and it begins quoting his source, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not check the needle's direction in the reticulum too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea of checking the needle's eye. With a needle in the wall of the בית הכוסות, we never check which way the eye faces.
steps.simpleTranslation: A needle found in the thickness of the wall of the בית הכוסות: if it sticks out on one side, the animal is כשרה; if it sticks out on both sides, it is טרפה. And we do not say, 'Let us see whether the eye faces outward or inward'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge that started on the previous page. It points to the rule of a needle in the wall of the בית הכוסות, where nobody checks which way the needle's eye is facing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא suggested that the direction of the needle's eye tells us where it came from. If the eye points outward, it may have entered from outside the organ, after piercing something else. But for the בית הכוסות, the הלכה simply depends on how far the needle goes through (one side or both sides), with no check of the eye. So why should the eye's direction matter anywhere else?

keyTerms.meaning: The reticulum, the second chamber of an animal's stomach
Thickness (here, inside the thickness of the stomach wall)
Kosher, fit to eat
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
The eye of a needle (the hole at the back end)

steps.confusionAlert: Even though this line sounds like a question, its job is a challenge. It uses the known rule of the בית הכוסות to attack the idea of checking the needle's eye.

phrases.english: [A needle found] in the thickness of the reticulum
if it goes through on one side, it is kosher
if it goes through on both sides, it is a tereifa
and we do not say
'let us see whether the eye faces outward'
'or whether the eye faces inward'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אָמְרִינַן לִיחְזֵי אִי קוֹפָא לְבַר אִי קוֹפָא לְגָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous page about using the needle's eye direction as evidence.
steps.kashyaTarget: The method of checking whether the needle's eye faces outward or inward
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the case of the בית הכוסות, the halacha ignores the eye's direction. That suggests the eye's direction is not real evidence of where the needle came from.

steps.title: In the stomach, food and drink can push the needle around
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the stomach is different. Food and drink pass through it and can push a needle into any position, so the eye's direction proves nothing there.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: There, since there is food and drink, we can say that the food and drink pushed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the בית הכוסות is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food and drink are always moving through the stomach and can shove a needle around. So even if its eye points outward, we can still assume the needle came from inside. In an organ with no food moving through it, the eye's direction still works as evidence, so the method stands.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that other case)
Food and drink
They pushed it

steps.whatToRemember: Checking the needle's eye is valid evidence, except in a place like the stomach, where food and drink can push the needle around.

phrases.english: They say: there
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of the בית הכוסות from the previous step.

phrases.english: since there are food and drink
say that the food and drink pushed it

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָתָם, כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא אֳכָלִים וּמַשְׁקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (the stomach has moving food and drink)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the eye's direction is ignored in the בית הכוסות, it might seem to be meaningless everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is ignored only in the stomach, where food and drink can push the needle. Elsewhere the eye's direction is real evidence.

steps.title: A needle in the liver's big duct: רבינא rules the animal kosher
steps.stepSummary: A needle was found in the large duct of a liver. One sage ruled the animal טרפה and another ruled it כשר. רבינא sided with the כשר ruling and said the ones who ruled טרפה must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: A needle was found in the large duct of a liver. הונא מר son of רב אידי declared it טרפה; רב אדא בר מניומי declared it כשר. They came and asked רבינא. He said to them: Take the cloak of those who declared it טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case of a needle found in the liver's big duct and how רבינא settled the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A needle inside the duct could have arrived through the natural passage, so finding it there does not prove the liver was pierced. רבינא held the animal was clearly כשרה. The sages who forbade it caused the owner a real loss and must pay for it, which shows how strongly רבינא held this.

keyTerms.meaning: A needle
The large duct (a main passage tube in the organ)
The liver
Declares it טרפה / declares it kosher
A cloak or robe

steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows that wrongly forbidding a kosher animal is not just being careful. It can cause a real loss to the owner.

phrases.english: There was a certain needle that was found
in the large duct of a liver

phrases.aramaic: הוּנָא מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי טָרֵיף
phrases.english: Huna Mar, son of Rav Idi, declared it a tereifa
Rav Adda bar Minyumi declared it kosher
They came and asked Ravina
He said to them
Take the cloak of those who declared it a tereifa
phrases.notes: Taking their cloak means they have to pay the owner for the kosher meat he lost because of their ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מַחְטָא דְּאִישְׁתְּכַח בְּסִמְפּוֹנָא רַבָּה דְּכַבְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theoretical discussion to a practical case of a needle in the liver.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A needle found in the large duct of the liver does not make the animal טרפה. Those who wrongly forbade it must pay for the loss.

steps.title: A date pit in the gallbladder came in through the duct
steps.stepSummary: A pit was found in a gallbladder. רב אשי reports that רב כהנא taught it surely came in through the duct, even if it seems too big to pass back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain pit was found in a gallbladder. רב אשי said: When we were at רב כהנא's house, he said: This certainly took the path of the duct and came in. Even though it does not come out, it slipped in little by little.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another real case, a pit found in a gallbladder, and רב כהנא's teaching that the animal is כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We assume the pit entered through the natural duct, not by piercing the gallbladder wall. A reader might object that the pit is too big to squeeze back out through the duct. רב כהנא answers that it slips through gradually with the body's movements, so it could still have come in that way.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit (of a fruit)
The gallbladder
It took (a path) and came
It surely slips through little by little

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'it won't come out now, so it couldn't have come in.' The גמרא says it slips in gradually, even if we cannot push it back out by hand.

phrases.english: There was a certain pit that was found in a gallbladder
Rav Ashi said
When we were in the house of Rav Kahana
he said
This certainly took the duct and came in
phrases.notes: The duct is the tube connecting the liver to the gallbladder.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא קָא נָפְקָא
phrases.english: Even though it does not come out
it surely slips through little by little

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא קְשִׁיתָא דְּאִישְׁתְּכַח בְּמָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another practical case, like step 3, this time about a pit in the gallbladder.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pit found in the gallbladder is assumed to have entered through the duct, so the animal is כשרה, even if the pit cannot easily be pushed back out.

steps.title: Only a date pit; an olive pit pierces
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רב כהנא's rule to a date pit. A pointed olive pit is assumed to have pierced the gallbladder.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies to a date pit, but an olive pit surely pierces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the rule in step 4: it applies only to a date pit, not an olive pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A date pit is smooth and rounded, so we assume it slid in through the duct. An olive pit is pointed, so we fear it pierced the gallbladder wall from outside, and the animal is טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: This statement (applies only...); introduces a limit on a rule
A palm tree (here, a date pit)
An olive
It surely pierces

steps.whatToRemember: A smooth date pit in the gallbladder: we assume it came through the duct, so כשרה. A pointed olive pit: we fear it pierced, so טרפה.

phrases.english: And this applies only to the pit of a palm
but that of an olive
surely pierces

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּדִיקְלָא, אֲבָל דְּזֵיתָא מִיבְזָע בָּזַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of step 4 to date pits only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The assumption that a pit entered through the duct applies only to a smooth date pit. A pointed olive pit is assumed to have pierced, making the animal טרפה.

steps.title: Why the lung is called ריאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the lung is called ריאה because it lights up (מאירה) the eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why is the lung called ריאה? Because it lights up the eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement from רבי יוחנן explaining the name of the lung through a wordplay. Eating lung is good for one's eyesight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Hebrew name ריאה sounds like מאירה, 'lights up.' This is not a הלכה about כשר or טרפה. It is a side remark about the lung's health benefit, and the next step will ask exactly how that benefit works.

keyTerms.meaning: The lung
Lights up, brightens

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Why is its name called 'rei'a' (lung)?
Because it lights up the eyes.
phrases.notes: A play on sounds: ריאה sounds like מאירה. The lung helps the eyesight of whoever eats it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָהּ רֵיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the gallbladder cases and returns to the topic of the lung.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lung is called ריאה because it brightens the eyes.

steps.title: Eaten plain or treated with substances?
steps.stepSummary: The Sages ask whether רבי יוחנן means the lung helps the eyes when eaten plain, or only when prepared with special substances.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Does it help when eaten as is, or only when treated with special substances?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about רבי יוחנן's statement and is setting up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן did not say how the lung helps the eyes. Either simply eating it works, or it only works after being treated with some kind of medicinal ingredients.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised among the Sages (an open question)
Substances, medicinal ingredients

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Is it for eating (as is),
or through treatment with substances?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: לַאֲכִילָה, אוֹ עַל יְדֵי סַמָּנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי יוחנן's statement works in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the lung help the eyes when eaten plain, or only when treated with substances?

steps.title: Proof from the price of a goose lung
steps.stepSummary: A goose costs one זוז but its lung alone costs four. If plain eating worked, people would just buy the goose. So the benefit must come from treating it with substances.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב הונא בר יהודה said, 'A goose sells for one זוז, and its lung for four.' If the lung helped just by eating it, a person would buy the whole goose for one זוז and eat its lung! So it must work through treatment with substances.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question using a market price. The lung is sold separately for much more, which only makes sense if it is prepared in a special way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody would pay four for a lung if one could get the whole goose, lung included, for one. The extra price must pay for the medicinal treatment. That shows רבי יוחנן meant a treated lung.

keyTerms.meaning: A זוז, a silver coin
If it enters your mind (if you think)
Rather (introduces the correct conclusion)

steps.whatToRemember: The lung helps the eyes only when treated with substances, proven by its high separate price.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
for Rav Huna bar Yehuda said:
A goose sells for a zuz,
and its lung for four.
phrases.notes: Four זוזים: the lung alone costs four times as much as the whole bird.

phrases.english: And if you think it means plain eating,
let him take the goose for a zuz and eat!
Rather, it is through substances.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lung helps the eyes only when treated with substances, as its high separate price shows.

steps.title: A hole where the butcher handled the lung
steps.stepSummary: If a lung has a hole exactly where the butcher's hand handles it, do we blame the butcher (making the animal כשר) or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the lung was punctured in the spot where the butcher's hand handles it, do we attribute the hole to him or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new, practical question about a hole in the lung and sets up the מחלוקת that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole in the lung from when the animal was alive makes it טרפה. But the butcher handles the lung after שחיטה and could have made the hole himself. The question is whether we may blame him and say the animal was fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Was punctured, got a hole
The butcher
We attribute it (blame the hole on a known cause)

steps.confusionAlert: תלינן here works in favor of the animal: if we blame the butcher, the hole happened after שחיטה, so the animal is כשר.

phrases.english: If the lung was punctured
at the place where the butcher's hand handles it,
do we attribute it to him, or not attribute it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינַּקְבָה רֵיאָה הֵיכָא דִּמְמַשְׁמְשָׁא יְדֵיהּ דְּטַבָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the lung's health benefit to a practical טרפה question about the lung.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a hole found where the butcher handled the lung be blamed on him?

steps.title: Two sages disagree about blaming the butcher
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר נתן says we blame the butcher; מר זוטרא son of רב מרי says we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר נתן said: We attribute it. מר זוטרא son of רב מרי said: We do not attribute it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two opposite answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר נתן trusts that the hole is in the exact place the butcher touches, so it likely came from him, and the animal is כשר. מר זוטרא does not rely on that and treats it as a real hole, so the animal is טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not attribute it (the hole counts as a real defect)

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר נָתָן אָמַר: תָּלֵינַן,
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Natan says: We attribute it,

phrases.aramaic: מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra son of Rav Mari says:
We do not attribute it,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר נָתָן אָמַר: תָּלֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two answers to the question in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחלוקת: רב אדא בר נתן says תלינן; מר זוטרא says לא תלינן.

steps.title: The הלכה: we blame the butcher
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רב אדא בר נתן: we attribute the hole to the butcher.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: We attribute it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the מחלוקת in favor of תלינן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the hole is right where the butcher handles the lung, we assume he caused it after שחיטה. So the animal is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The final הלכה, the practical ruling

steps.whatToRemember: A hole in the lung where the butcher's hand touches it is blamed on the butcher, so the animal is כשר.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: We attribute it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: תָּלֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opinions of step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הלכה: תלינן. The hole is blamed on the butcher and the animal is כשר.

steps.title: Support from רבי אבהו's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל son of רבי אבהו reports that his father, a leader of רפרם's כלה lectures, ruled תלינן, and he refused to accept מר זוטרא's opposite view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל son of רבי אבהו said: My father was one of the heads of the כלה lectures of רפרם, and he said: We attribute it. They told him the view of מר זוטרא son of רב מרי, and he did not accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds support for the הלכה of תלינן from an important teacher's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו held a leading teaching role and ruled תלינן. When רב שמואל heard מר זוטרא's stricter view, he rejected it. This backs the ruling given in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Heads of the כלה, the big public study sessions
He did not accept it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel son of Rabbi Abbahu said:
Father was one of the heads of Rafram's kallah lectures,
and he said: We attribute it.
They said it before him,

phrases.aramaic: לְהָא דְּמָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי,
phrases.english: this view of Mar Zutra son of Rav Mari,
phrases.notes: This is the opinion from step 10 that we do not blame the butcher.

phrases.english: and he did not accept it.
phrases.notes: Meaning רב שמואל rejected it and stuck with his father's ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אַבָּא מֵרֵישֵׁי כַּלֵּי דְּרַפְרָם הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the הלכה of step 11 and rejects מר זוטרא's view.
steps.raayaObject: The הלכה that תלינן (blame the butcher).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבי אבהו, a head of רפרם's כלה, and his son's rejection of מר זוטרא's view.

steps.title: Blaming the butcher is like blaming a wolf
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא says logic supports his grandfather רב אדא בר נתן, since we already blame holes on a wolf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: It makes sense to follow my grandfather's view, because we already blame holes on a wolf.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא gives a logical support for the ruling that we blame the butcher's hand for the hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a wolf carried off meat and we find a hole, we say the wolf made it and the animal stays כשר. The same logic applies to the butcher: when there is an obvious outside cause, we blame it. This strengthens the הלכה already set like רב אדא בר נתן.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it is logical
My father's father (my grandfather)
We attribute / we blame (the damage on a known cause)
Wolf

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
It makes sense to follow my grandfather's view,
phrases.notes: His grandfather is רב אדא בר נתן, who said in step 10 that we blame the butcher.

phrases.english: since we attribute holes to a wolf.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּוָותֵיהּ דַּאֲבוּהּ דְּאַבָּא מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a logical support to the ruling in Steps 11-12.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that we blame the butcher for a hole where his hand touches.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The accepted rule that holes in meat taken by a wolf are blamed on the wolf.

steps.title: Dispute about a worm hole in the lung
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר דוסאי and the רבנן argue whether a worm came out of the lung before or after שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a worm: רב יוסף בר דוסאי and the רבנן argue. One says it came out before the שחיטה; the other says it came out after the שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another 'who do we blame' case: a hole made by a worm leaving the lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worm came out before שחיטה, the animal had a hole while alive and is טרפה. If it came out after שחיטה, the hole happened to dead meat and the animal is כשר. The argument is about which timing we assume.

keyTerms.meaning: A worm
They argue
It came out / left
Before the slaughter

phrases.english: A worm,
phrases.notes: He means a worm that bored out of the lung and left a hole.

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר דּוֹסַאי וְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Dosai and the Rabbis argue about it.
One says: it came out before the slaughter,
and one says: it came out after the slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּרְנָא, פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר דּוֹסַאי וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case of attributing a hole to a later cause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two opinions: the worm left before שחיטה (טרפה) or after שחיטה (כשר).

steps.title: Ruling: the worm came out after slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that the worm left after שחיטה, so the animal is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: it came out after the שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the worm dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We assume the worm made its hole after the animal was slaughtered. So the hole does not make the animal טרפה. This fits the pattern of blaming the later, outside cause.

keyTerms.meaning: And the practical law is
After the slaughter

steps.whatToRemember: We blame a hole on an outside cause when one is clear: the butcher's hand, a wolf, or a worm that came out after שחיטה.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: it came out after the slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: לְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה פָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the dispute in Step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A worm hole in the lung is presumed to have formed after שחיטה; the animal is כשר.

steps.title: How deep must the hole go for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון from the משנה and explains that he means a hole reaching the large airway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: until it is pierced. רבה בר תחליפא said in the name of רב ירמיה בר אבא: until it is pierced into the large airway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and explains exactly what רבי שמעון meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון says a lung hole makes the animal טרפה only when it reaches the airways. רב ירמיה בר אבא clarifies: it must reach the main, large airway, not just a small branch.

keyTerms.meaning: Until it is pierced through
The large airway in the lung (main bronchus)
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse this with the first opinion in the משנה: there, any hole in the lung is enough to make it טרפה. רבי שמעון is more lenient.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: not until it is pierced.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, where he says the hole must reach the airways.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Tachlifa said
that Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said:
Until it is pierced into the large airway.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁתִּינָּקֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'who to blame' topic and returns to the משנה's dispute about lung holes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the hole must reach the large airway to make the animal טרפה.

steps.title: A report that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אבא, sitting before רב הונא, reports in the name of רבי מלוך and רבי יהושע בן לוי that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר אבא sat before רב הונא and said: רבי מלוך said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone reports a ruling on רבי שמעון's view. This sets up רב הונא's correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this report were right, the lenient view of רבי שמעון would be the practical law. The ruling is passed down through רבי מלוך from רבי יהושע בן לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Sat before him (learning in his presence)
The law follows (the view of)

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Abba sat before Rav Huna,
and he sat and said:
Rabbi Malokh said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רבי שמעון to asking whether we rule like him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reported ruling: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רב הונא corrects the report
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that מלוך the Arab actually said the הלכה does NOT follow רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to him: Are you quoting מלוך the Arab? He says the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא rejects the report and gives the correct version of what מלוך said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling was quoted backwards: the real tradition from מלוך is 'אין הלכה כרבי שמעון'. So this report cannot be used to rule like רבי שמעון. The final ruling only comes in step 23, after another tradition in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי appears in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: The Arab (a nickname, maybe from where he lived)
The law does not follow

steps.whatToRemember: The correct tradition is that the הלכה does NOT follow רבי שמעון about lung holes.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said to him:
Are you quoting Malokh the Arab?
He says the halakha does not follow Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַלּוּךְ עַרְבָאָה קָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the report in Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole reported ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The report reversed מלוך's words; he actually said the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רב ביבי repeats the report that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: When רבי זירא came up to ארץ ישראל, he heard רב ביבי teaching in the name of רבי מלוך and רבי יהושע בן לוי that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא went up to ארץ ישראל, he found רב ביבי sitting and teaching: רבי מלוך said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about the same report we just saw in Step 17. This sets up a challenge to that report in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17, רב אחא בר אבא gave this same report, and רב הונא disputed it. Now רב ביבי in ארץ ישראל is teaching it too, so the question of what רבי מלוך really said comes up again.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up, meaning moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל
The practical law follows רבי שמעון

phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira went up,
phrases.notes: "Went up" means he moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he found Rav Beivai
who was sitting and saying:
Rabbi Malokh said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סָלֵיק רַבִּי זֵירָא, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַב בִּיבִי דְּיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same report rejected by רב הונא in Step 18 comes up again through רב ביבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ביבי reports, in the name of רבי מלוך and רבי יהושע בן לוי, that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבי זירא testifies that רבי מלוך himself denied it
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא swears that he and two other אמוראים asked רבי מלוך in person. רבי מלוך told them he had said the הלכה does NOT follow רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: By your life, I, רבי חייא בר אבא and רב אסי visited רבי מלוך's town and asked him, 'Did you say the הלכה follows רבי שמעון?' He told us, 'I said the הלכה does NOT follow רבי שמעון.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא rejects רב ביבי's report with first-hand testimony from רבי מלוך himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up רב הונא's claim in Step 18. The person being quoted denied the quote directly, in front of three witnesses, so this version of the tradition falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: By the Master's life, a strong oath-like way to say 'I swear this is true'
We happened to come to, we visited
His place, his town

phrases.english: He said to him: By the Master's life,

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲנָא וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא וְרַב אַסִּי
phrases.english: I and Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba and Rav Asi
happened to come to the place of Rabbi Malokh,
and we said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמַר מָר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: Did the Master say the halacha follows Rabbi Shimon?
And he said to us:
"The halacha does not follow Rabbi Shimon" is what I said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חַיֵּי דְּמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the report in Step 19 with direct testimony.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The report in רבי מלוך's name that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי מלוך himself said the opposite, so the report quoted him wrongly.

steps.title: What else do you have on this?
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי asks רבי זירא what other tradition he holds on this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you, what do you have in your hand on this?
steps.whatsHappening: A short question that asks for any other tradition on the issue. It sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the רבי מלוך chain has been taken apart, the question is whether some other report of רבי יהושע בן לוי's view exists.

keyTerms.meaning: What is in your hand, meaning what tradition do you have

phrases.english: And you, what do you have in your hand?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַתְּ מָה בִּידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבי זירא's rejection by asking for another source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether any other tradition reports רבי יהושע בן לוי's view on רבי שמעון.

steps.title: A different chain says רבי יהושע בן לוי does follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The answer quotes רבי יצחק בר אמי, who reports in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יצחק בר אמי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: A second chain of tradition is given, and it does support the ruling for רבי שמעון in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבי מלוך chain was shown to be wrong. Still, רבי יהושע בן לוי's position in favor of רבי שמעון survives through a different person, רבי יצחק בר אמי. So there are now two opposing views that still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he said

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַמֵּי
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ami said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יצחק בר אמי reports in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Final ruling: the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון. Any hole in the lung's membranes makes the animal a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final ruling on the lung argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though one tradition of רבי יהושע בן לוי supports רבי שמעון, the practical ruling goes against him. So a hole does not need to reach a large airway to make the animal a טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The law is not like that view
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even after proper שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון. Any hole through the lung membranes makes the animal a טריפה, even if it does not reach a large airway.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for checking the lung, after a long back-and-forth over the traditions.

phrases.english: And the halacha does not follow Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the competing traditions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is against רבי שמעון. Any hole in the lung's membranes makes the animal a טריפה.

steps.title: כהנים treated the fat on the abomasum as permitted
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case of a pierced קֵבָה, רבי אושעיא reports that כהנים treated the fat on the קֵבָה as permitted, following רבי ישמעאל. A memory hook is given to help remember this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If the קֵבָה was pierced.' רבי יצחק בר נחמני said in the name of רבי אושעיא: the fat on the קֵבָה, the כהנים got used to treating it as permitted, following רבי ישמעאל, who said it in the name of his fathers. Your memory hook: 'ישמעאל the כהן helps the כהנים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה, the pierced קֵבָה, and brings a related ruling about the fat on top of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a debate about whether the fat on the קֵבָה counts as forbidden חֵלֶב. The כהנים, who received the קֵבָה as one of their gifts, followed רבי ישמעאל's lenient view and ate it. The memory hook ties רבי ישמעאל, himself a כהן, to rulings that help כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: The קֵבָה (fourth stomach, the abomasum) was pierced, a case from the משנה
Forbidden fat
They got used to treating it as permitted
Your memory hook, a phrase to help you remember

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up קֵבָה (the stomach part, which כהנים receive as a gift) with the question of the fat on top of it. The leniency is only about the fat on the קֵבָה, not about any other חֵלֶב.

phrases.english: The abomasum was pierced.
Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Oshaya said:
Fat that is on top of the abomasum,
the priests got used to treating it as permitted,
following Rabbi Yishmael, who said it in the name of his fathers.
And your memory hook:
"Yishmael the priest helps the priests."

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיקְּבָה הַקֵּבָה. אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fat on the קֵבָה was treated as permitted by כהנים, following רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: Where does רבי ישמעאל help the כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the memory hook refers to, meaning where else רבי ישמעאל helps the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind the memory hook. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A memory hook only works if we know a familiar case where רבי ישמעאל favors the כהנים. The גמרא now asks for that case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it, asking which case is being referred to

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the background to the memory hook in Step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The case in which רבי ישמעאל is known to favor the כהנים.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: ה׳ blesses the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל learns from the פסוקים of ברכת כהנים that the כהנים bless ישראל, and הקדוש ברוך הוא blesses the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'So shall you bless בני ישראל.' רבי ישמעאל says: we learned about a blessing for ישראל from the mouth of the כהנים, but we did not learn about a blessing for the כהנים themselves. When the פסוק says 'And I will bless them,' this tells us that the כהנים bless ישראל and הקדוש ברוך הוא blesses the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא showing a place where רבי ישמעאל reads the פסוק in a way that benefits the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל reads 'and I will bless them' as referring to the כהנים, so the כהנים also get a blessing, straight from הקדוש ברוך הוא. This is the well-known example of רבי ישמעאל 'helping the כהנים', and it makes the memory hook make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: The priestly blessing
And I will bless them (במדבר 6:27)
You must say, this shows that

steps.whatToRemember: The memory hook works because רבי ישמעאל is known for readings that favor the כהנים, like his teaching that ה׳ blesses the כהנים. That helps us remember that the lenient ruling on the fat of the קֵבָה is his.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"So shall you bless the children of Israel"
Rabbi Yishmael says:
We learned of a blessing for Israel from the mouth of the priests,
but for the priests themselves we did not learn.
When it says, "And I will bless them,"
you must say:
The priests bless Israel,
and the Holy One, Blessed be He, blesses the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: כֹּה תְבָרְכוּ אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25 by naming the case behind the memory hook.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ישמעאל teaches that 'ואני אברכם' means הקדוש ברוך הוא blesses the כהנים, which is his well-known reading in favor of the כהנים.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the כהנים bless and God agrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads 'וַאֲנִי אֲבָרְכֵם' as referring to ישראל. The כהנים bless ישראל, and הקדוש ברוך הוא agrees to their blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: We already learned that the כהנים bless ישראל, but we did not yet learn that God blesses ישראל. When the פסוק says 'and I will bless them,' it means: the כהנים bless ישראל, and God agrees to their blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step goes on and gives רבי עקיבא's opinion. He argues with רבי ישמעאל about who 'them' is in 'וַאֲנִי אֲבָרְכֵם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל read 'them' as the כהנים, so God blesses the כהנים. רבי עקיבא reads 'them' as ישראל. In his view the פסוק teaches that God backs up the blessing the כהנים give, not a separate blessing for the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: From the mouth of the Almighty, meaning from God Himself
'And I will bless them', the last words of the ברכת כהנים section
You must say. It introduces the only reading that works
Agrees through them, meaning God approves and backs up their blessing

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
We learned of a blessing for Israel from the mouth of the כהנים,
but from the mouth of the Almighty we did not learn.
When it says 'and I will bless them' —
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:27. For רבי עקיבא, 'them' means ישראל, not the כהנים.

phrases.english: you must say: the כהנים bless Israel,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַסְכִּים עַל יָדָם.
phrases.english: and the Holy One, Blessed be He, agrees to their blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second, opposing opinion within the same ברייתא quoted in step 26
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In 'וַאֲנִי אֲבָרְכֵם', 'them' is ישראל. God agrees to the blessing that the כהנים give.

steps.title: Where does רבי עקיבא learn a blessing for the כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי עקיבא uses 'וַאֲנִי אֲבָרְכֵם' for ישראל, what source does he have that the כהנים are blessed?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי עקיבא: where does he learn that the כהנים receive a blessing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי עקיבא's source that the כהנים get a blessing too. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא already used the פסוק that רבי ישמעאל used for the כהנים' blessing. The גמרא assumes the כהנים do get blessed, so it asks where רבי עקיבא learns that.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it? A request for a source
A blessing for the כהנים

phrases.english: But Rabbi Akiva,
a blessing for the כהנים, from where does he know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּרָכָה לְכֹהֲנִים מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what follows from רבי עקיבא's reading in step 27
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי עקיבא's source for a blessing given to the כהנים

steps.title: From 'I will bless those who bless you'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that רבי עקיבא learns it from 'וַאֲבָרְכָה מְבָרְכֶיךָ': whoever blesses ישראל is blessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: From the פסוק 'And I will bless those who bless you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives רבי עקיבא's source. God promised אברהם that whoever blesses his children will be blessed, and the כהנים bless ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the כהנים bless ישראל, they fall under God's promise to bless those who bless ישראל. So רבי עקיבא agrees that the כהנים are blessed, only from a different פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And I will bless those who bless you', God's promise to אברהם

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
From 'And I will bless those who bless you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא learns the כהנים' blessing from 'וַאֲבָרְכָה מְבָרְכֶיךָ'

steps.title: So how does רבי ישמעאל help the כהנים more?
steps.stepSummary: Both opinions agree that the כהנים are blessed. So in what way is רבי ישמעאל specially helping them?
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does he help the כהנים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the memory hook from step 24, which said רבי ישמעאל helps the כהנים. If רבי עקיבא also gives them a blessing, what extra help does רבי ישמעאל give?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 showed that both תנאים agree the כהנים get a blessing. That seems to remove what makes רבי ישמעאל special, which is the whole point of the memory hook.

keyTerms.meaning: Helps or supports
The כהנים (Aramaic form)

phrases.english: And in what way does he help the כהנים?
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי ישמעאל, from the memory hook in step 24.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי מְסַיַּיע כָּהֲנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 29 to question the memory hook
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי ישמעאל is the one who helps the כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא also gives the כהנים a blessing, so רבי ישמעאל seems to add nothing special.

steps.title: Same פסוק, same blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל puts the כהנים' blessing in the same פסוק as ישראל's blessing, so their blessing equals ישראל's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he places the blessing of the כהנים in the same place as the blessing of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל gives the כהנים a better kind of blessing. It comes straight from the ברכת כהנים section itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the כהנים are blessed only in a general way, like anyone who blesses ישראל. For רבי ישמעאל, the blessing comes in the same place as ישראל's blessing, so it is as full as theirs. That is why he is the one who 'helps the כהנים'.

keyTerms.meaning: Places or sets up (a reading)
In the place of, here meaning in the same פסוק as

phrases.english: Because he places the blessing for the כהנים
in the same place as the blessing of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמוֹקֵי לֵהּ לְבִרְכַּת כֹּהֲנִים בִּמְקוֹם בְּרָכָה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a difference in the quality of the blessing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both תנאים give the כהנים the same blessing, so רבי ישמעאל adds nothing
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל puts the כהנים' blessing alongside ישראל's in the same section, so it is a fuller blessing
steps.whatToRemember: The memory hook works because רבי ישמעאל 'helps the כהנים'. He gives them a blessing in the same פסוק as ישראל's, and he also permits them the fat on the קֵבָה.

steps.title: What did רבי ישמעאל say in his fathers' name?
steps.stepSummary: Back to the main topic: what is רבי ישמעאל's statement, said in the name of his fathers, that the כהנים relied on to permit the fat on the קֵבָה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל, who spoke in the name of his fathers: what is his statement?
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion about the memory hook is done, and the גמרא goes back to רבי אושעיא's report from step 24. It asks what exactly רבי ישמעאל's ruling is, and this sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said the כהנים permitted the fat on the קֵבָה following רבי ישמעאל. Now the גמרא wants to see the actual source of that ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of his fathers, a tradition passed down in his family
What is it? A request to identify a statement

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, who said in the name of his fathers:
what is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם אֲבוֹתָיו מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the memory hook discussion and returns to step 24
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of רבי ישמעאל's ruling permitting the fat on the קֵבָה

steps.title: The ברייתא begins: 'all the fat on the innards'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that explains the פסוק listing the forbidden fat 'that is upon the innards'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: 'All the fat that is upon the innards'…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a ברייתא. It opens with the פסוק about forbidden fat, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's ruling will come from how this פסוק defines which fat is forbidden. So far only the opening words of the פסוק have been quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat
The innards

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'All the fat'
that is upon the innards'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:3. The ברייתא keeps going after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא אֶת כׇּל הַחֵלֶב אֲשֶׁר עַל הַקֶּרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 32
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא explaining the פסוק of 'הַחֵלֶב אֲשֶׁר עַל הַקֶּרֶב' (still in progress)
